body:
## The shape

`playwright.config.ts` sets `fullyParallel: true` with `workers: 2` in CI. Each
`test.describe` is serial *within itself*, but different describes go to different
workers — so up to two specs run at once, and they draw from the same seeded
library.

That library is small. CI seeds 5 EPUBs (`tests.yml`), two of which are the 2 KB
RTL/LTR fixtures, so **exactly 3 clear `reader-notes.spec.ts`'s 60 KB floor**:
`alice_in_wonderland`, `christmas_carol`, `metamorphosis`. There are 6 reader
spec×project combos competing for those 3 books, and `tag-merge-delete.spec.ts`
mutates library state on the same seeded books.

The reader specs call `clearAnnotationsViaApi` before their first render — correct
hygiene against a crashed previous run, and actively destructive when another
spec is mid-test on the same book.

## Evidence, from three sessions, none of it conclusive alone

1. **A note read back with the wrong timestamp** (CWNG NEW5). The popup contained
   `"…Frame narrative established here. 1786378802615"` — a real note, from a
   *different run*. So the spec tapped a stale or foreign annotation. That is
   shared-fixture contention, not a broken feature.
2. **`socket hang up` on `POST /api/v1/books/6/metadata`** and `GET /api/v1/tags`
   in `tag-merge-delete.spec.ts` (CWNG FRONTEND) — the server dropping connections
   mid-test rather than a UI timing problem. Book 6 is in the seeded set.
3. **`tag-merge-delete.spec.ts:109` failing, then passing on a control run with an
   unchanged head** (341 vs 343 passed). Flaky, not a diff.

Same hazard, three presentations: a wrong value, a dropped connection, a varying
failure.

## What has already been done, and what it does not cover

`reader-notes.spec.ts` now rotates its book choice per spec rather than
partitioning by stride — the stride version could select *nothing* for higher
offsets on a 3-book library, which was a separate and deterministic bug
(`F-943f51`). Rotation gives distinct starting points and full fallback, and is
strictly better than what `main` had before (every spec on one book).

**It does not eliminate the hazard.** With 6 combos over 3 books, two concurrent
specs can still land on the same fixture. Rotation lowers the probability; it does
not make sharing impossible.

## Options, none taken yet

- **Seed more books.** Cheapest, and it widens every lane at once. The floor
  exists to skip fixtures with no prose, so the new books need real text.
- **Give each spec its own fixture**, uploaded in a `beforeAll` and deleted after.
  Strongest isolation; costs ingest time per spec.
- **Stop clearing the whole book.** Capture a baseline, assert deltas, and delete
  only the rows the spec created — `restoreAnnotations` already does exactly this
  for teardown, so only setup is destructive. Would make a collision harmless
  rather than rarer, which is the better property.
- **Serialise the mutating specs** against each other rather than globally.

The third is probably right, and it is the one that removes the class rather than
reducing the odds. Not attempted here because it touches specs across more than
one owner's surface and wants doing deliberately rather than under a red CI.
title: e2e specs share a 3-book seeded library under fullyParallel, so concurrent specs clear each other's fixtures
